preamble: The voiceless retroflex stop [ʈ] is lenited to the voiced retroflex flap [ɽ] between vowels. In Tamil, voicing is not contrastive in native vocabulary, and a single (non-geminate) retroflex obstruent written ட is realized between vowels as either a voiced stop [ɖ] or a flap [ɽ], while the voiceless stop [ʈ(ː)] is kept for the orthographic geminate ட்ட. Yele (Yélî Dnye), a Papuan isolate of Rossel Island, likewise reduces /ʈ/ to a flap [ɽ] between vowels.
